expected_failure_policy: Roots are often stems whereas reflexes are inflected lexemes. Exact-word failures are retained; learned alignments and certificate validity do not supply missing morphology.

normalization.dropped_accent_limitation: These baselines cannot model Verner conditioning and must not be described as doing so.
normalization.reflex_policy: Use the source Phonemic_Segments column verbatim; no orthographic-to-phonetic inference. Reject opaque aliases/uncertainty tokens. Raw columns remain in corpus.json.
normalization.root_policy: Remove reconstruction star and morpheme hyphens; u̯/i̯ become w/j; subscript laryngeal numbers become ASCII; acute lexical accent is dropped. Retain length, palatal and aspiration distinctions. Parse all explicit comma/tilde alternatives or reject the entire expression. Unspecified H and optional segments remain unsupported.

source_uncertainty.source_comment: Indirectly attested in the form of (LÚ)kuu̯an- 'hound-man'. We have included *kuu̯an- / kun- as the best currently-known potential candidate based on parallel vocabulary (cf. Melchert 1989, EDHIL s.v.), while at the same time we acknowledge that due to the fragmentary attestation of Hittite a more suitable target lexeme may also have existed.
< IE *eh3uiom, cf. Arm jvoj (gen.) and Cze vejce. Orel, however, claims it to be a loan from Latin. Both have same etymological origin, however.
acc. sg. (but nom. sg. would be identical), stem probably āiia-

Linked with Skt. meghá- m. 'cloud, gloomy weather', Av. maēɣa- m. 'cloud', Gr. ὀμίχλη 'mist, fog', Lith. miglà 'fog', Dutch dial. miggelen 'staubregnen', etc. Other scholars consider it a loan < Iranian.
Cf. Ion. τέσσερες, West Greek τέτορες, Homeric πίσυρες, Boeotian, Thessalian πέτταρες.

Instrumental plural noun attested in PY Ta 722.2. Generally interpreted as καρα(h)α(π)-φι or κρᾱ(h)α(π)-φι < *kra(h)at-pʰi < PIE *kr̥h₂sn̥t-pʰi (cf. Hom. κρᾱ́ατα). The transcription is tentative: /k(a)ra(ː)(h)a(p)pʰi/
Together wirh Gr. κρᾱνίον, Ved. śīrṣṇá- going back to PIE *k̑roh₂sno- 'head'.
From PAlb *enmen- or *inmen-, etymologically close to OIr ainm, Slav *jbmę, PRus emnes, all meaning the same, and to other continuations of IE *(o)noHmn.
Cf. CHD L-N 31-36 for attestations and discussion
The vocalism points to PIE acrostatic *h₁nḗh₃-mn̥ > PToch. *ñemə, but other cognates are consistent with a proterokinetic paradigm.

Nom.sg.com. form attested by Sumerographic writing GIBIL-aš. The native script form *ne-e-u̯a-aš has been reconstructed from the attested accusative form ne-e-u̯a-an. Cf. CHD L-N 455-458 for attestations and discussion.

Fem. we, cognate with Toch. B wi (both genders).

Adverbial form. As an adjective the numeral is otherwise only attested using the logographic spelling '2' taking case endings from the pronominal declension, cf. Hoffner & Melchert (2008:156). Cf. EDHIL 826-827 s.v. tān 'for the second time, again, subordinately' for examples of forms attested and discussion.
AV ~ bhásma n. AV+ SHOULD BE EARLY VEDIC SWADESH TERM, on which see [cognate set 2189](cog-2189).The Sanskrit word is a thematicized form from the full grade stem of the PIE root noun.

The lexeme is normally spelled using the Sumerogram GÌR (Akk. ŠĒPU), e.g. nom.sg. GÌR-aš. The native script form given, pa-a-tu-u[š] is acc.pl. Also attested are instr. pa-te-et, gen.pl. pa-ta-a-an, and dat.-loc.pl. pa-ta-a-aš. According to Kloekhorst (2008:653-654) the OH forms may reflect the original athematic root noun, while the thematic pata- forms attested in NH are secondary innovations. Cf. CHD P 231-235 for attestations and further discussion.
Ultimately from a derivative *pod-yo-; cf. Toch. B paiyye. Du. peṃ., pl. peyu, peñ* (acc. pes).
Middle English knowen, Old English cnāwan
Root /knā-/, cf. Toch. B /nana-/ 'appear'. Significantly less common than /krsā-/, but no clear evidence for secondary or restricted value; also clearly inherited.

reference_pool_scope: All parsable published roots in the frozen sample, including test references. This is declared closed-set retrieval, not generation of previously unknown ancestors.
split_policy: No development/test pairs fit mappings. Published sources and model training may already contain these etymologies; no blind-discovery claim.
vocabulary_policy: The frozen corpus defines a shared symbol inventory; no held-out token frequencies or correspondences are fitted.
